summary: Rotator cuff repair in beach chair with an interscalene block ordered on the right in a patient with a paralyzed LEFT hemidiaphragm (phrenic injury after thoracotomy). An interscalene block would paralyze the other side.

asa.rationale: Moderate OSA, obesity, unilateral diaphragm paralysis with restriction, HTN with LVH.

decision.recommendation: proceed with a diaphragm sparing analgesic plan
decision.rationale: Do not perform an interscalene or supraclavicular block. Use suprascapular (anterior or posterior) plus axillary nerve block, or surgeon infiltration, with multimodal analgesia.

redFlags.finding: Contralateral hemidiaphragm paralysis with interscalene block ordered
redFlags.evidence: Left phrenic injury 2020; PFT supine FVC drop 22%, MIP -58; orthopnea; SpO2 94% flat.
redFlags.implication: Interscalene block blocks the right phrenic nerve nearly always, causing bilateral paralysis and respiratory failure.
redFlags.action: Cancel interscalene; suprascapular and axillary nerve blocks or local infiltration.

redFlags.finding: Beach chair with hypotensive anesthesia request
redFlags.evidence: 70 degree sitting; surgeon wants hypotension; untreated BP 158/94 with LVH.
redFlags.action: Measure or correct BP to the brain level, keep MAP near baseline, avoid deliberate hypotension, consider cerebral oximetry.

planItems.item: GA with ETT plus diaphragm sparing block
BP referenced to brain level; consider arterial line or cerebral oximetry
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Beach chair with head neutral and padding
